title: bn254-pairing-inversion via GT DLP tightened Floyd Pollard-rho (130.868186)

claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial 32-adding Floyd Pollard-rho algorithm in proof.md recovers the GT discrete logarithm x with g^x=z and returns the pairing preimage P=P0 and Q=[x]Q0, satisfying e(P0,[x]Q0)=g^x=z with both points in the order-r subgroups, at exploratory success probability at least 0.50, using at most 2^130.868186 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) and at most 2^20 bytes of peak total storage. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic, supported and limited in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. The uniform capped instruction bound is 2*ceil(sqrt(r))*167936 + 2^40, holding on every run with no run gate or unbounded subroutine; the one-time scalar multiplication [x]Q0 and the subgroup checks [r]P=[r]Q=infinity are charged under the 2^40 setup allowance (machine.md). Total work includes all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, hashing, arithmetic, memory access, recovery, verification and output. This reduces pairing inversion to the GT discrete logarithm; no prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or production-scale attack execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check full-width four-word Montgomery arithmetic, run the actual 32-adding Floyd walk on four small cyclic groups including failures, verify the protected BN254 generator order and the exponent-label invariant on full-width Fp12 elements, and recompute the itemized cap and rounded-up score. These are finite walk-statistics and correctness evidence; they do not prove production success.
